name: The man gathering sticks on the Sabbath
charge: Gathering sticks on the Sabbath day to kindle a fire: the presumptuous sin
summary: The sabbath had already been given as the sign between the Lord and Israel, and its breach already carried death. The law had just separated the sin of ignorance, which an offering covered, from the sin done presumptuously, which is a man thinking about it before he does it; the man found gathering sticks is the example the chapter gives. He was held in ward until the manner of the death was declared, and all the congregation stoned him. The fringes were given in the same breath, so that Israel would look and remember.
offenseFull: Israel was to keep the Lord’s sabbaths, for it was a sign between Him and them throughout their generations, so that they would know that He was the Lord who sanctified them; everyone who defiled it was surely to be put to death, and anyone who did work on it was to be cut off from among his people (Exodus 31:13-14, 15). It is more than a day of rest; it is the sign of who the God of Israel is. No fire was to be kindled throughout their habitations on the sabbath day (Exodus 35:2, 3), and kindling fire goes to cooking: what was to be baked was baked the day before and the rest laid up, for the sabbath food is cooked the day before (Exodus 16:23).

The chapter sets the two sins side by side. If a soul sinned through ignorance, without knowing what he was doing, he brought a she goat of the first year, the priest made an atonement for him, and it was forgiven him, and one law covered the man born in Israel and the stranger alike (Numbers 15:27-29). But the soul that does anything presumptuously, whether born in the land or a stranger, reproaches the Lord and is cut off from among his people; because he has despised the word of the Lord and broken His commandment, that soul is utterly cut off, and his iniquity is on him (Numbers 15:30-31). Presumptuously means wilfully: he thought about it before he did it, and there was no offering written for that. While the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the sabbath day (Numbers 15:32). He is the example of the sin just described. He was not picking up sticks for the sake of sticks; he was

gathering them to kindle a fire and cook on a day he was commanded to rest. He never even reached the act; he had the intention, and the case stands as a warning against every man excusing his own trade on that day.
judgmentFull: Those who found him brought him to Moses and Aaron and to all the congregation, and they put him in ward, which is to say they locked him up, because it had not been declared what should be done to him: the fact of the death was already written, and the manner was what was sought (Numbers 15:33-34). The Lord told Moses that the man was surely to be put to death, all the congregation stoning him with stones outside the camp; and all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the Lord commanded Moses (Numbers 15:35-36). He was killed without mercy, and he was made an example.

Because of that act the Most High gave Israel the fringes: they were to make fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, with a ribband of blue on the fringe, so that they would look on it and remember all the commandments of the Lord and do them, and not seek after their own heart and their own eyes, after which they used to go astray (Numbers 15:37-41). The fringe is worn on the border where it can be seen. When a man thinks of sin he looks at the fringes and remembers the law, instead of going out and picking up sticks.

The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and the mercy is not a licence. Anyone who despised the law of Moses died without mercy under two or three witnesses; of how much sorer punishment is the man counted worthy who has trodden the Son of God underfoot and used the grace period to stay in the same sin (Hebrews 10:28-29). The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel, and the Son of man is Lord of it, so that it is lawful to do well on that day and grace is given for what is out of a man’s control, never for what he plans (Mark 2:27-28; Matthew 12:8-12).

lawsResolved.text: Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

text.text: Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying, Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep: for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the Lord that doth sanctify you.

Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death: for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
Six days may work be done; but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord: whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.
Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord: whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.
Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.

And he said unto them, This is that which the Lord hath said, To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the Lord: bake that which ye will bake to day, and seethe that ye will seethe; and that which remaineth over lay up for you to be kept until the morning.
And if any soul sin through ignorance, then he shall bring a she goat of the first year for a sin offering.
And the priest shall make an atonement for the soul that sinneth ignorantly, when he sinneth by ignorance before the Lord, to make an atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.
Ye shall have one law for him that sinneth through ignorance, both for him that is born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.
But the soul that doeth ought presumptuously, whether he be born in the land, or a stranger, the same reproacheth the Lord; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
Because he hath despised the word of the Lord, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.
And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man that gathered sticks upon the sabbath day.
And they that found him gathering sticks brought him unto Moses and Aaron, and unto all the congregation.
And they put him in ward, because it was not declared what should be done to him.
And the Lord said unto Moses, The man shall be surely put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.
And all the congregation brought him without the camp, and stoned him with stones, and he died; as the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue:

And it shall be unto you for a fringe, that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and that ye seek not after your own heart and your own eyes, after which ye use to go a whoring:
That ye may remember, and do all my commandments, and be holy unto your God.
I am the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the Lord your God.
He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:

Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.
And when he was departed thence, he went into their synagogue:
And, behold, there was a man which had his hand withered. And they asked him, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days? that they might accuse him.
And he said unto them, What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out?
How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
